note: Commitments extracted verbatim from Realize Vision 2050 (Mayor's Task Force, Oct 23 2025; transmitted to Council Dec 2 2025). STATUS IS NOT ASSERTED. Each row records the commitment, its stated due date, and whether a public record of completion has been located. 'no_public_record' means exactly that and nothing more - not that the work did not happen.

updated_vision_statement.text: Our City is an eco-city. Our streets are significant contributors to our resilience, which should incorporate technologies such as sustainable, permeable surfaces that work with nature. All City departments and partner agencies coordinate seamlessly to manage infrastructure as one interconnected system. Greenery, native flora, and urban wildlife are fully and rightfully integrated into the city's design, making Berkeley a living ecosystem where infrastructure and nature thrive together. The City maintains systems that enable continuous adaptation of infrastructure to evolving fire safety, traffic safety and climate resilience needs, ensuring a safe and sustainable future for all.

top_five_actions.title: Have a Unified Approach Across City Departments and Other Agencies
Prepare an Infrastructure Program Plan
top_five_actions.detail: by Spring 2026, with an updated CIP and the next budget; prioritization using Envision criteria, to address the $2+ billion of infrastructure needs

top_five_actions.title: Implement an Asset Management Program (AMP)
top_five_actions.detail: life cycle maintenance management; condition assessment started and NexGen asset management software fully implemented

top_five_actions.title: Gain Support for New Funding
top_five_actions.detail: Council should discuss polling and funding options for a measure in 2026 or 2028

commitments.text: Prepare a master schedule for preparing and updating planning studies
Prepare a new policy for post-disaster reconstruction complying with the City's climate action goals
Department heads to coordinate planning during annual budget reviews
Establish collaboration with U.C. Berkeley and U.C. Davis
Prepare a plan to incorporate new technologies, emphasis on green infrastructure, in the implementation of Measure FF

commitments.goal_title: Implement a life cycle maintenance management program
commitments.text: Establish an AMP steering committee, including the Mayor's office, City Manager's office, the FITES Policy Committee and subject matter experts

commitments.goal_title: Implement a life cycle maintenance management program
commitments.text: Begin condition assessment of infrastructure systems
commitments.note: The report states condition assessment work has started and NexGen software is fully implemented, so this may be partly met; no public milestone record located.

commitments.goal_title: Implement a life cycle maintenance management program
commitments.text: Implement an AMP for facilities, street paving, sidewalks and sewers

commitments.goal_title: Implement a life cycle maintenance management program
commitments.text: Prepare an annual maintenance plan by Q1 of each fiscal year, and a report of maintenance work completed by the following Q1
City Council to conduct polling to evaluate public support for funding infrastructure improvements
City staff to develop a long-term strategy for the City's bonding capacity and the scheduling of issuing bonds
Complete an Infrastructure Program Plan, to prioritize funding needs and consider organizational requirements
commitments.note: Named as top-five action B. The Mar 19 2026 memo from task force members states the Program Plan was not implemented as of that date.

commitments.text: City Council to discuss a funding measure in 2026 or 2028
commitments.note: A $300M infrastructure GO bond was placed on the November 2026 ballot, which satisfies the discussion commitment. Whether it followed the prioritization the same report calls critical is the open question.

commitments.text: Initiate public tours of infrastructure projects, and hold a tour once a quarter
Hold a public kickoff meeting for Measure FF
Develop a strategy to utilize social media more effectively
Initiate an annual report to the public of public works success stories

recommended_next_actions.text: Inform Council of the Realize Vision 2050 Implementation Plan
Communicate with applicable commissions and Council Policy Committees (FITES, HLEECS, and seven named commissions)
Consider a ballot funding measure in 2026 or 2028
recommended_next_actions.lead: Mayor Ishii, with City Council and City Manager

recommended_next_actions.text: Form a core team led by the Public Works Director to implement the recommended actions; progress reports to Council and commissions annually or as needed
recommended_next_actions.note: This is the commitment that would have produced a status record for every other row on this page. No such progress report has been located.

the_dream_in_their_words.framing: Picture yourself standing on a street corner in Berkeley in 2050. What will our city look like? Will our infrastructure adapt to make our lives safer, more productive and enjoyable?
elements: protected, pothole-free bike lanes wide enough for first-responder access
a safe streets initiative (Vision Zero) that changed bike and pedestrian safety
an accessible electrified shuttle, in its 20th year of operation
restored wetlands buffering the waterfront against sea-level rise and storm surge
a bustling ferry terminal at the Marina
solar and wind producing a significant portion of city power
Fire Department conducting neighborhood defensible-space inspections ahead of Diablo winds
the_dream_in_their_words.closing: over the past 30 years, the city started implementing long-term changes that make such a positive impact to our quality of life
the_dream_in_their_words.usage_note: This is the City's own dream scenario, written by its own task force. Ways Forward should quote it rather than compose one. A campaign that writes the utopia owns the pathos; a campaign that quotes the City's utopia and sets it beside the City's own calendar is doing logos with the City's own material.

status_legend.met: A public record of completion exists.
status_legend.apparently_met: A public event satisfies the commitment on its face.
status_legend.no_public_record: The due date has passed and no public record of completion has been located. This is a statement about the public record, not about the work.
status_legend._warning: Statuses here are researched from public sources, not confirmed with the City. Every 'no_public_record' row should be put to the City before publication, and the reply published alongside it.
